description: Primary-source regulatory facts for the toner corpus's version of issue #16 (FDA-allowed vs internationally banned). Scope is deliberately narrower than the foundation corpus's regulatory.json: it covers the salicylic acid concentration limit (the one rule this corpus's own active ingredient actually triggers) and the same EU-declarable fragrance allergen list already verified for foundation. It does NOT repeat foundation's full EU Annex II general-prohibition sweep (checking every one of this corpus's ~50 distinct ingredient names against all 1760 Annex II entries) -- that is a several-hour hand-verification exercise in its own right, not yet done for this category, and is recorded as an open gap rather than silently assumed clear. See data/manifest-toner.json known_limits and the MoCRA timeline, which is shared across every corpus in this project and lives at data/regulatory.json rather than being duplicated here.

salicylic_acid_limit.eu_annex: Annex III entry 98 (substances cosmetic products must not contain except subject to the restrictions laid down)
salicylic_acid_limit.instrument: Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009, as amended by Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/1966
eu_conditions: Not to be used in preparations for children under 3 years of age.
Not to be used in applications that may lead to exposure of the end user's lungs by inhalation.
Not to be used in oral hygiene products.
Non-preservative use must be evident from the product's presentation.
salicylic_acid_limit.us_monograph: 21 CFR Part 333, Subpart D (topical acne drug products), OTC monograph

source.type: Consolidated EU legal text; amending regulation
source.publisher: EUR-Lex, Publications Office of the European Union
source.note: Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/1966 of 27 November 2019 replaced Annex III entry 98 with the table cited here, applicable from 2020-05-01. This corrects an easy-to-make error: an earlier amending regulation, 2019/831, is sometimes cited for these figures, but it addressed CMR classification, not this concentration table.

salicylic_acid_limit.note: A facial toner is a leave-on, non-excluded-category product, so the EU ceiling (2.0%) numerically matches the US OTC monograph ceiling this corpus's products are filed under. The EU rule carries one condition the US monograph does not: a ban on use in preparations for children under 3. None of this corpus's labels carry an age restriction, so a 2%-labeled US product would need that condition addressed, not just the concentration, to be Annex-III-compliant if sold in the EU.

fragrance_allergens.note: Same 26-substance EU-declarable list already verified for the foundation corpus (data/regulatory.json fragrance_allergens.eu). Every toner product in this corpus declares its scent only as generic 'fragrance' or 'parfum' rather than naming an individual allergen, so the computed match against this corpus is 0 for all seven products -- see data/regulatory-analysis-toner.json.
